name: Myanmar
summary: Yellow, green and red horizontal bands with a large white five-pointed star in the centre. It was introduced in 2010 under the constitution drawn up by the military government, replacing the flag used since 1974.
origin: After independence from Britain in 1948, Burma's flag was red with a blue canton holding a large white star and five small stars. The socialist government of 1974 replaced the stars with a cogwheel and rice plant surrounded by fourteen stars.

The 2008 constitution, written under the military government, specified a new flag, which was raised on 21 October 2010, shortly before elections. The design recalls the flag of the Japanese-backed State of Burma during the Second World War, which used the same colours with a peacock.

facts: The old flags were ordered to be burned when the new flag was introduced in 2010.
Pro-democracy movements have used other flags, including a red flag with a fighting peacock.
Lithuania's flag uses the same three colours in a different order, without the star.
